scope: Independent chronological selection/editorial review; source-specific repeat and concentration dispositions, not a measured popularity ranking or an exhaustive article-body factual audit.

decisions.changed_angle: The May2 Stocktwits earnings, raised-outlook and extremely-bullish retail-mood item was already used in May5. The proposed secondary is 150 whitespace/152 regex words, preserves the evidence and execution risk, and adds no fictional new catalyst.

CNBC's May6 IPO investment-gain feature is new since the May6 report cutoff. It changes the attention angle from May5 operating news to realized-wealth framing, with the weak outlook retained as the counterweight. Frequency alone does not require rotation.

The May6 wealth feature and May5 weak-outlook/collaborations item were available to the prior May7 edition. The proposed unchanged thesis is a 150 whitespace/160 regex-word secondary; it does not claim a new operating catalyst.

Hims remains relevant after the price move but has no new post-May7-cutoff retail source. Keep only the proposed 150 whitespace/160 regex-word secondary, with customer economics and commercial terms rather than another full partnership essay.

BRK.B and BRK-B are the same Class B shares. The May6 CNBC dip-buying and May5 succession sources repeat May7. The generic May7 Buffett advice quotation did not create a new company catalyst. Replace the duplicate lead with a 150 whitespace/160 regex-word Berkshire carryover.

The May8 proposed convertible offering and CTO appointment are new since the May8 cutoff, shifting the item to financing and organizational execution. The offering remains proposed, not cash already raised; the concentration diagnostic is not a quota.

The May15 UBS upside forecast and weaker-dollar argument are new since the prior May14 gold appearance. The item keeps them as prospective views and distinguishes bullion/fund exposure from mining operating risk rather than claiming achieved returns or measured retail inflows.

The May21 CNBC/Reuters all-time-high event and record-attention interpretation are fresh. Bitcoin can lead on that own-date development even though three assets overlap the previous basket; unchanged D-Wave and Tesla items are shortened separately. No forced basket rotation is justified.

The May20 system launch already supported the May21 D-Wave lead. The proposed 150 whitespace/159 regex-word secondary keeps the existing launch thesis and updated market risk without treating a price update as a new technology milestone.

The May21 Reuters weaker-dollar/geopolitics coverage supports a continuing secondary hedge alongside speculative equity and token trades. This is a limited insurance-role discussion, not another lead essay or a claim of new structural demand or measured retail buying. Frequency alone is not an exclusion rule.

Musk's May20 five-year leadership pledge already appeared in May21. The proposed 150 whitespace/157 regex-word secondary retains the founder-focus thesis while requiring demand and delivery evidence; no rhetorical repetition is promoted into a new catalyst.

IonQ has a company-specific May22 platform ambition and share-response attention, distinct from D-Wave's system launch and Rigetti's approach. The lead attributes the Nvidia comparison to IonQ's CEO rather than treating separate quantum businesses as interchangeable beneficiaries.

CNBC's May22 further record is an eligible continuation-attention event. The secondary explicitly frames breakout retention and implementation risk; it does not rebuild the previous full Bitcoin lead or imply that exchanges, miners and treasury companies provide identical exposure.

The own-date silver-upside commentary supports a separate smaller catch-up trade, explicitly an investment argument rather than observed buying. Silver and gold belong to one family but have different industrial sensitivities, and the item warns that nominal price does not establish value.

The May23 renewed EU/Apple tariff threats are fresh after the prior May22 gold cutoff and change the policy-risk setting. The earlier downgrade source remains background. A measured bullion hedge can persist without a forced asset quota or a claim of new gold flows.

The May23 ABC retirees-in-crypto story and May25 reported ownership comparison are new demographic/audience evidence since May23. The prose attributes the claims, treats them as attention rather than guaranteed buying, and keeps token exposure distinct from company wrappers.

The only cited May21 Reuters dollar/geopolitics source predates the May26 gold cutoff. The proposed 150 whitespace/157 regex-word secondary retains insurance and portfolio-sizing discipline without presenting an unchanged catalyst as a fresh demand story.

Gold's repeated insurance role does not require removal, but unchanged evidence calls for brevity. The proposed carryover is secondary, 150 whitespace/157 regex words, with tariff-negotiation risk and fund/miner distinctions retained.

The May26 cheaper-China-chip plan and Wednesday earnings preview were already used in May27. The proposed secondary is 150 whitespace/160 regex words, keeps results pending at midnight and avoids turning the pre-result rally into evidence of a beat.

Trump Media's May27 proposed financing for bitcoin is a new corporate-wrapper event after May26, with an adverse share response in CNBC's headline. The financing is a proposal and does not establish completed token purchases or equivalence between DJT shares and spot bitcoin.

The May28 Fed-minutes inflation/recession-risk headline is new since May27; the May26 Singapore custody story adds a separate attributable angle. The item remains a proportionate hedge and does not translate wealthy-investor custody choices into a measured universal retail view.

The May29 global chip rally after results, Dell outlook increase on AI demand and contrary analyst view are fresh after May29. The lead changes from pre-result anticipation to completed market reaction and downstream demand, with options products distinguished from their different payoff structures.
